data.name: Shobharam
data.long_meaning: Shobharam means one who is radiant and beautiful. It is derived from the Sanskrit words shobhana (beautiful) and rama (pleasing). The name is often used to describe someone who is auspicious and elegant.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shobharam is a name that evokes a sense of the divine. It is often used to describe someone who is beautiful in the eyes of God and radiates inner and outer beauty.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Shobharam carries a 6 Personal Year Cycle. This is a cycle of idealism and expansion, where growth is sought after. It is a time of heightened personal and spiritual awareness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shobharam holds great cultural significance in Hinduism. It suggests an aesthetic sense and an appreciation for the beauty of the world around us. It is also associated with the ideals of purity, grace, and charm which are valued greatly in Indian culture. The name adds a touch of elegance and sophistication to any person who bears it.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Shobharam signifies the inner beauty and radiance of a soul. It is a reminder that true beauty lies not in external appearances, but in the inner qualities of a person. It encourages one to strive for inner peace, purity, and self-realization. The name is also seen as a reminder of the divine presence and the beauty of nature. It is believed that by calling upon the name of Shobharam, one can invoke a sense of peace, serenity, and divinity within oneself.

historical_references.reference: Shobharam was a renowned Hindu monk and philosopher who lived during the 13th century in India. He was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement, which emphasized the devotional aspect of Hinduism. Shobharam is best known for his works on the philosophical concepts of love and devotion towards god, particularly Bhagavad Bhakti.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Shobharam is found in the famous Indian epic, the Mahabharata. In this context, Shobharam is mentioned as a great sage and a disciple of Vyasa, the author of the Mahabharata. He is said to have lived during the period of the Kurukshetra war, around the 9th or 10th century BC.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata, disciple of Vyasa, great sage
